analysis: The changed security behavior is in .github/workflows/provider-signing-validation.yml. A new `identity` step (head lines 64-76) in the build job runs tooling/scripts/provider_release_identity.py against the candidate checkout. It writes APP_NAME, CLI_NAME, ENCLAVE_NAME, PRODUCT_*_NAME and DARKBLOOM_RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT to $GITHUB_ENV and $GITHUB_OUTPUT. The signing job (lines 118-121) imports these as env and uses them in the codesign, entitlement-extraction, notarize and staple paths (lines 171, 181, 191, 194, 198-199, 216). Those steps run with the Developer ID .p12, provisioning profile and notarization credentials. The script itself was not supplied, so whether it validates name shape and rejects newlines is unverified. The `unpack` step checks the app against unsigned-files.json produced by the same build job, so it is not an independent check. Hard-coded literals remain for io.darkbloom.fan-helper, darkbloom-fan-helper and mlx.metallib. The fan-helper entitlements and requirement still use the fixed Team ID. Coverage limits: .github/workflows/ci.yml was supplied as head text only, with no patch, so its diff was not isolated. I saw no new secrets, no broadened permissions (contents: read) and no pull_request_target. Actions are SHA-pinned in the visible lines. .github/workflows/release-swift.yml and the first signing-validation unit were metadata-only, so the release workflow changes were not reviewed. The integration pass should look at release-swift.yml and at provider_release_identity.py, and check that the same identity values reach the production release signing job. No threat-model text needs updating from what was visible.

findings.detail: The new `identity` step in the build job runs `provider_release_identity.py --source candidate`, which reads the identity file from the candidate commit. Its output is written to both `$GITHUB_ENV` and `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`. The signing job (`needs.build.outputs.*`) then uses APP_NAME, CLI_NAME and ENCLAVE_NAME to build filesystem paths and codesign targets, for example `$RUNNER_TEMP/signing-stage/$APP_NAME` and `$app/Contents/MacOS/$CLI_NAME`. The signing job also writes the decoded provisioning profile into `$app/Contents/`. This runs while the Developer ID certificate, profile and notarization credentials are loaded. The names were previously hard-coded. The step guarantees only that the verified commit signature check passed, not that the source was reviewed. The visible workflow does not show validation of these values for path separators, `..` or newlines before they reach `$GITHUB_ENV` and the signing steps. If `provider_release_identity.py` accepts such values, a candidate source file could redirect the profile write or the signing and verification targets outside the stage directory, or inject extra environment variables. The `unpack` check compares the app against the build-produced `unsigned-files.json`, which comes from the same candidate-influenced values, so it adds no independent check. Fix: have the script enforce strict allow-list patterns (single path component, `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+`, no newlines). Alternatively re-derive or re-validate the names in the signing job from trusted tooling rather than from build outputs.
findings.title: Signing job uses candidate-derived names for paths and codesign targets without visible validation
